utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, Mr. Kovacic. Witness, on page 46, line 3 and 4, you said that: "All bridges were designed to be destroyed." In French you said -- you used the word "prepared." So when the bridge was built was everything put in place so that the bridge could be easily destroyed? Is that what you meant? Or after the bridge was built were explosive devices and cords positioned on the bridge, as it seems to be the case? If it was done during the construction, is the Old Bridge -- was the Old Bridge in such a situation? Because the bridge was built long before the JNA.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to repeat once again that I was in the technical services, I was mostly in charge of our artillery. Officers working technical services were talking with one another and we knew that bridges were prepared to be destroyed. What I know is that preparation was such that we were expecting the enemy to come from the west. So we were supposed to be activated from the east side. That's what I know. I also know that as far as recent constructions are concerned, the army asked the builders to take into account the place where the explosive would be positioned. As for the old bridges, I don't know. How was it done, I do not know. That's all I know. The rest would be speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We know that in Mostar all the bridges were destroyed, that the Old Bridge was not the only bridge in Mostar. Unless I'm mistaken - and please correct me if I'm wrong - it seems that bridges were destroyed during the conflict with the Serbs. Therefore, certain bridges were destroyed by the Serbs. From a technical point of view, is it possible that the Serbs had positioned explosive charges on all the bridges so that nobody can see them, and for one reason or another they didn't blow up those bridges. Maybe the explosive charges remained as well as the detonating cords. Is it possible that accidentally or voluntarily one device was activated, a device that would have been positioned there not by the warring parties but by a third party? Is that possible from a technical point of view?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This idea occurred to me as well. All I can say is that it is possible from a technical point of view, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a slightly different question. I would like us to be as complete as possible. When a stone construction is deconstructed by using an explosive device, it is possible to find on the stones traces of explosives. Did anybody look at it, according to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, nobody looked for it from what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certain stones that fell into the water are probably still there, or were all the stones taken out of the river?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. The bridge was reconstructed, I know that. I know that the stones were taken out of the river, the bridge was not complete so more stones had to be added.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is a stone in the water after an explosion took place, does the water wash away the traces of explosives or can it stay there and is it possible that years later, with all the technical means at our disposal, we can find traces of TNT, syntax, or other explosive devices?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not think so. After an explosion there is no more explosives; you have gas instead. Having stayed in the water for a long period of time, I don't think you would have found such traces. I did not look for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think Mr. Praljak wanted to intervene because this is a technical matter.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the benefit of the Chamber, because you asked him about reactions, I want to tell you how it was for me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, the Trial Chamber reminds you that you cannot testify. Maybe your Defence counsel can provide us with this information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to tell the Chamber that the book you spoke about, 10.000 copies were printed of this book, I sent it to UNESCO and I sent it to everyone precisely in order to cause this kind of reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm done basically, but based on the Chamber's questions I do have another question that I can't avoid asking. There was a reference to the possibility that the JNA earlier on had, in a manner of speaking, set the bridge up for destruction. What about the fuse that was under the water? What would be its expected water life, in a manner of speaking? Would it last a full seven days, 700 days perhaps, seven years? Would that technically be feasible?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise answer, but the detonating cord can remain in the water for a certain period of time. How long, I don't know. Maybe my colleagues who are specialists in that field could answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You can't tell us more than you know. I've checked the transcript about all these questions, and can we please have again the slow-motion recording of the Mostar, the Mostar TV video-clip, and just tell us again, Professor, because I'm not entirely certain it was faithfully reflected in the transcript. As for the continuity of this recording, the Mostar recording, does it tally with the continuity seen in the ORF footage and is it continuous in terms of time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: This is just the critical moment, as it were, just before the destruction and the collapse itself. Does this tally with the ORF2 footage which we have so far been referring to as the principal footage?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I would even say that the Mostar footage is the most important because it shows a continuity. There is the water gush, and right after, the collapse of the bridge. I have viewed it several times, and it is very important because there is continuity. The movements that we can see are those of someone handling the camera. From one frame to the next, the changing of the way objects are positioned tally with the movements by a man. It doesn't come from two different cameras, not at all. So in my view this is the most relevant document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... footage. If it were not for that footage, I would not be here today because there is no continuity in the first footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Kovacic. There might be a video-clip that I would like to see --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You took the words right out of my mouth. I wanted to go back to your initial question. We identified the exhibit, this is P 01040, 01040, for the transcript, that was witness Delalic, showing the scenes that I believe you referred to, the projectiles actually hitting the bridge. But I think this should be time that was allowed for your questions because my time is over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could we view video-clip P 10040 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, just for the sake of time, the Prosecution expects to play that videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We might as well see it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that there is another video, IC 574.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] Your Honours, we don't have it prepared. We retrieved it, but perhaps we might make a small break for the registry to do it. But I would like to draw your attention to the first part of this recording where you can see the impacts of the shells. It's clearly marked as the 8th of November, for -- so it is irrelevant for the purposes of our discussion today because it shows the situation on the 8th of November, and according to the indictment the bridge was destroyed on the 9th. So that's why we have those recordings that show just a couple of frames, just a few frames or just a few seconds before the bridge actually collapsed. So we don't have this video with this IC number prepared, but I'm sure that the registry should be able to retrieve it given some time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar has found it, so we will view it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, while we're looking for it I didn't want to interrupt the proceedings, but my colleagues have told me that there is an error in the transcript. I'm not quite sure whether it is an error or not, I think it is. May I ask a follow-up question to the witness. It's at page 45, line 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So first of all, let me say after a brief explanation that I will read at line 14, Professor Jankovic said, this is discussion with Professor Hartmann, and there is a sentence, the concluding sentence, where Professor Jankovic says as follows: [In English] "With respect to the destruction of the bridge by projectiles, we both agree." [Interpretation] The question was asked by Judge Prandler about this letter and this view, and then the witness replied with respect to the effects of projectiles, the effects on the bridge. [In English] "I can say that the shelling damaged the bridge. Professor Hartmann, I think, that is my opinion after viewing the recordings, the damages were -- the damages occurred on the constructions added to the bridge and those constructions were totally destroyed. The bridge itself was damaged. I do not know which term to use. It is better not to be too precise. I believe that Professor Hartmann is not qualified to talk about the destruction on the bridge caused by projectiles." [Interpretation] And the transcript is accurate. And then we come to the sentence that I read at the beginning. [In English] "With respect to destruction of the bridge by projectiles, we both agree." So the question is, Professor Jankovic, whether "we both agree" refers to Judge Prandler and yourself or to you and Hartmann or should it not read explosives rather than projectiles or does this wording "both agree," does it include what Judge Prandler said or something else? So could you please explain this. The introductory part is quite clear and it is obvious that the final sentence follows from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could perhaps the registry print out page 45 for the benefit of the witness so that he can look at it. Well, obviously it doesn't work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So could you please say what you said.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I may repeat it. As far as I'm concerned with respect to the destruction of buildings by explosives, Professor Hartmann is undeniably extremely qualified and in that respect, our views tally, we think the same. But what I'm saying is that Professor Hartmann knows nothing about projectiles, the impact of projectiles, he's not qualified to talk about the destruction of the bridge by projectiles. He's perfectly able to watch the footage, to view the footage, and to make comments about it. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I think that now it is quite clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The registrar was not in a position to play IC 574, the Defence cannot do it either, but the Prosecutor can play it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's precisely the footage I wanted to view.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have to rewind because the screen was not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we have to rewind and to start from the beginning. Professor, please watch this footage very closely. The quality is much better than what we've seen so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's remind you that the date of this footage is the 8th of November and not the 9th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Professor, you viewed this footage. We seem to have footage from the 8th and from the 9th. On the 8th, we see shells hitting the bridge and damaging the bridge, parts of the bridge collapse into the water, and at the end of the footage we see the collapse of the bridge. This is a video of a far better quality than what we saw before. Does that change your conclusions in any way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I believe that the second part of the footage is exactly the same as what we saw before, and the beginning of the footage shows the damage caused by a shelling on the bridge. And we see that the constructions that were on top of the bridge have been completely destroyed. You see tiny houses that had been built on the bridge, and at some point you see very clearly how these small houses disappear. You see part of these small houses falling into the water. Maybe that was the aim of the shelling, to destroy these constructions, but it's obvious when watching the footage, serious damage is being caused on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we talk about the footage from the 8th of November, we get the impression that we see tracing bullets, at least we see a red light on the footage. What is it according to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that you're right, these are tracing bullets or tracer bullets. I think that we see the projectile in the footage. You can't film that sort of scene without seeing the projectiles, there's no doubt about it, and here we see these tracer bullets. It's something I was not aware of, actually, but -- because if you don't have tracer bullets it's more difficult to make out the projectiles on a footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You've laid out your theory before us. You've viewed that footage frame by frame. You've looked at the 25 frames preceding the collapse of the bridge, and during this period of time you did not see any shell hitting the bridge. If you had used that technique for the footage of the 8th of November where we see that shells are hitting part of the bridge, then on each frame we would have seen the projectiles, wouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we would have. Yes, precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One brief technical question. Professor, had you seen this last video-clip before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we had seen it, but we concluded that this footage did not provide any specific information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, I don't think you have much time left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just a very brief question. You raised a very interesting issue and the answer we received was quite interesting, so I think we should follow up on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Professor, when His Honour Judge Antonetti asked you a question you described in some detail the damage to the superstructure of the bridge, and you say that at one point you can see the little piece, a little piece of the little houses built on the bridge falls into the water. Let me ask you this: As a citizen of the former Yugoslavia, not as a soldier, not as an expert, but did you see this bridge at one point?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Professor -- well, and I have to testify now because I myself saw this bridge, this is a notorious fact. But at any rate, there was no superstructure on this bridge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. I walked over that bridge several times because that's -- that's the bridge on the way to the sea and we would stop in Mostar just to walk on the bridge and there was nothing at the time on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, these little houses on the bridge, what are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know. I had never seen them before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask you an incidental question. You were an officer in the JNA, you left the JNA with the rank of lieutenant-colonel, you were trained as an officer. And as part of that training, were you taught the difference between buildings or constructions such as bridges that you can attack if they are military constructions or were you -- and were you taught about buildings or constructions that cannot be attacked because they are not military objectives? Is this part of a training of any military officer, and talking about tank crews, I believe that the one leading the tank crew - you can confirm that for us, talking about the JNA -- although here we are not talking about the JNA, but in the JNA, wasn't an officer always required to lead the crew, the crew of the tank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I received my training as a soldier in Brussels at the Polytechnic school and the technical school in Brussels, so I was trained as a soldier in Belgium. And based on that training I can tell you that at that time in Belgium there was always an officer, an engineer, just as me, who would command the tank. There was an officer, engineer, highly trained officer. Unfortunately, I know that in the army of the former JNA it was not the case. It's a subject, it's a topic, that I discussed time and time again. Training technically speaking was not sufficient, and I'm not even talking about solely technical training, but military training was not sufficient when it came to tank commanders in the former JNA. I'm aware of that. We had countless discussions about this at the time when I was still an officer. That's one thing. Secondly, my career was more of a technical career than of a military career, so it -- I would find it difficult to tell you exactly how you select a target. But when you have enemies in a given construction, when you have military enemies in a given construction, that construction becomes a target. But, yes, believe me, I'm a technician. I'm not a high-ranking officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Kovacic, I'm being told by the registrar that you've used up your time, but if you have one last question of course you may put it to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to formally conclude my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Professor, thank you for coming here, thank you for testifying. As you know, after the break, I assume you will be cross-examined by the Prosecution. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Let me now turn to the other Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, 6D does not have any questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. 6D, no questions. 5D?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have any questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4D.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we don't have any questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D we know already. 2D.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. And 1D?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Prlic's Defence has no questions for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. The best is probably to have a break before the cross-examination. It's half past 5.00. We'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The hearing's resumed for the cross-examination. You may proceed, Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Professor. My name is Kim West, and I am an attorney for the Office of the Prosecutor and I'm going to ask you some follow-up questions regarding your direct testimony. And in order to ensure that we're all on the same page I want to start with your written opinion in Exhibit 390328 [sic], and that's the opinion that you issued for this case. The English version is page 14 and the B/C/S is page 12.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have the official documents before me. I have my own documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the Prosecutor has a file and you'll be able to look them up.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the Prosecution's binder also contains the defendant's -- the accused's exhibits so this will go faster. So I'll direct your attention to page 14 of your report.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Croatian? Page Croatian?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Page 14 of the English, page 12 of the Croatian. Is that the page entitled "opinion"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So I'll direct your attention to -- under "Opinion," it's part (a) and you wrote: "There is a high probability that the Old Bridge has not been destroyed by attacks of gun tanks, but by a detonation of the explosive charge (or mine-explosive means) which have been placed in the bottom part of the bridge arch. The activation of the charge itself has been done through a detonating cord which has been activated from the close vicinity of the Old Bridge. This happened most probably from the left, respectively, the east bank of the Neretva River." Do you see that part of your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And indeed, that is the conclusion that you and your colleagues came to; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: In regard to the term that you used, you said "there is a high probability," on direct examination you explained that you and your colleagues discussed it and you came to the conclusion that that would be the term and those would be the words that you used. Why is it that you didn't use stronger language? Why didn't you use the words "high likelihood"?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: When we analysed the technical events, as a rule we have to be very cautious. It could happen, and it happened to me, that you have an explanation for a technical event, an explanation that is absolutely fair and compatible, and I repeat, is absolutely compatible, with the effects that we can observe but it is not to be ruled out that there would be another explanation which is equally compatible --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So if you --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: -- so you have to be cautious.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us then what factors -- can you tell us which factors of the videos that you watched made you not use stronger language?

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think that there's an area of uncertainty, at least to my mind, from my learned friend's questions. Is it the Prosecution's contention that high likelihood signifies a higher gradation of probability than high probability which is the witness's evidence. If a scale is being put forward, perhaps that can be articulated by my learned friend and put to the witness whether or not he agrees with that gradation from high probability to low probability, otherwise we're mixing oranges and apples it seems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I supplement that by saying that my reaction was very much the same as Mr. Khan's. I didn't see the difference in English, but more importantly because I checked with my colleague Mr. Lazic and Ms. Alaburic and they tell me that the translation into the witness's language produces the same meaning for either phrase. So clearly we English speakers only are puzzled, but what's very important is that the witness understands. If there is some gradation that means anything to him, then we've got a basis for the question; otherwise, we simply don't have any basis for this line of questioning at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: If I may just complement, I've just looked it up in the dictionary. In German it's the same, the translation is the same for both terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I look at the witness's testimony, from line - we're about to lose it - it's line 9 through 14. There may have been confusion among people in the courtroom, but he was not confused because he concluded that probability was less than likelihood if you read his answer in context, but I'll go ahead and ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, do you understand when I say high likelihood to be stronger language than high probability?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's speak in mathematical terms then. The three of us did not mention that, but I personally, I would say that this probability for this explanation is over 80 per cent, 0.8, that's what I would say.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And what did the other two [indiscernible]?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they're not here to give their opinions.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this question --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: However, I believe that we shared the same opinion, we agreed. There was no problem, there was no difference, no difference in opinion among ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, if you move on to 3(b) of your opinion, there you note what you reviewed in order to come to that opinion and I'm going to read that. It says: "A detailed study of the recordings of the TV ORF2 and TV Mostar, which have recorded the aforementioned events immediately before and during the destruction of the Old Bridge itself, point to this conclusion ..." Do you see that language?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's the item (b), isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, Professor, expert witness, I understood that when you say that it is highly probable you referred to mathematics, and that's the reason why you used this word which is not by chance because if you used it there must be a reason for using it. In other words, there must be a slight doubt prevailing in your opinion, otherwise you would have said it is certain that the Old Bridge was not destroyed by gun or tank guns or it is nearly certain that it was not destroyed by the tank gun. If you say that it is highly probable, that means that you do not rule out another reason or cause other than the tank shell. So what would have destroyed the Old Bridge is the explosive charge, as you indicated, but then why don't you write, We are 100 per cent sure that the explosive charge is the cause on account of the three factors, the light, the smoke, and the water fountain, which establish in a scientific manner that the Old Bridge was destroyed by this explosive charge. Why do you not reach 100 per cent conclusion, since you said 80 per cent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm going to tell you why. We said this in this very text. We believe 100 per cent that it is this water fountain that is caused by the explosion of the detonating cord, but we also saw that this transcript -- the recording was actually cut into two bits. If you did not have had the other bit that showed that it really happened that way, we would have said there was a water fountain but we do not know why the bridge fell. But thanks to the other footage we can see this continuity and we can reach our conclusion, but all this drives us to be cautious and this is absolutely normal in our practice. We call that reverse engineering. We must be cautious at all times. I can tell you -- I told you that we could find an explanation that fully tallied with the phenomenon, but we could also find another explanation that is also in agreement with the phenomenon. Therefore, prudence is the word. This is the reason why we choose this terminology. And we add that we are based on the recordings. We did not see it with our own eyes, we did not carry out on-site research. There are a lot of things that we haven't done.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: -- the videos upon which you based your opinion, there were two videos. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: The TV ORF2 video and the TV Mostar video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, is it your testimony that they are, in fact, different recordings from different angles but of the same event?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I've been thinking about this. Are we talking about the same event filmed by the Mostar cameras and the ORF2 cameras? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So when you look at the Mostar camera and you see a water splash before the bridge collapsed, my question: Is that the same water pillar or water wall that you see in the TV ORF video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: This is precisely what I said earlier on. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, let me direct you back to your opinion, and if you go to the English version and go to page 5, and that's also page 5 of the B/C/S. Right in the middle your -- this is the description of the TV ORF video, but the last sentence of that paragraph you write: "These happenings are even better visible on video recordings of TV Mostar as shown in picture 4." Professor, doesn't that suggest that at the time you wrote this opinion you believed them to be the same event just different vantage points?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I do believe it is the same event, but believe and certify, that's two different things.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: You've testified on direct at page 24, it was line 1, when you were speaking about the two videos. You commented that you saw the explosion and the water pillar in the two recordings, and you cited them as TV ORF and TV Mostar, although I understand that your belief or certification, those are different words. But my question is: For the basis of your opinion, did you rely on them to be the same event?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we thought it was the same event and we still believe it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Just to be clear, you were provided these videos by the accused; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And did Mr. Praljak also tell you they were of the same event or did you come to that conclusion on your own?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't remember that he gave me any such instruction. I think that this is a conclusion we drew ourselves, on our own.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you some questions in regard to timing, and I'm going to go back to your opinion. It's page 14 of the English, page 12 of the B/C/S, again we're going to the area under the heading of "Opinion." And in part (b), in talking about the TV ORF and TV Mostar you wrote: "These two videos have recorded the aforementioned events immediately before and during the destruction of the Old Bridge itself," and that they "point to this conclusion." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And so a key to -- one of the key points to your opinion was that the bridge came down into the water, collapsed, after you saw the water pillar and the explosion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I said that we had the light spot that we saw on the ORF video, but we could not see it on the TV Mostar video because it is overexposed so you can't see any light spot. After the light spot, we saw the water gush or pillar and the black smoke; that was on both videos.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And so again my question just so we're clear, that one of the key points to your opinion was that the bridge came down into the water, collapsed; after you saw the water pillar, then the explosion and the light part that you just point out, the key is that it then collapsed into the water. Correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you are now using the word "explosion." We saw the light spot. We saw the black smoke and we saw the water pillar, and thereafter the bridge collapsed. These events can be seen continuously in the TV Mostar footage; and I repeat it, this is the reason why that footage is the more important.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. So please go to page 3 of your opinion, in English and in B/C/S. In the top paragraph, sentence in the middle it says: "We have taken out two sequences from the received video documentation which show that the destruction of the bridge and the happenings which immediately preceded the destruction of the bridge." I used the term "immediately preceded." Again, does that show that a part, a key part, of your opinion had to do with timing?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. And if you go to the bottom of that page, the last paragraph per sentence: "However, the recordings on picture two of TV ORF 2, which immediately precede the destruction of the Old Bridge itself, indicate another possible conclusion ..." Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Which was the page?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, the same page. It's page -- yeah, page 3 in the English.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And at the very bottom -- you see that small paragraph at the very bottom that begins with: "However ..." In that sentence it says, "... the recordings on picture 2 from TV ORF 2, which immediately precede the destruction of the Old Bridge ..." Again my question to you is: That's another indication that timing was important to you, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to now direct your attention to Exhibit P 10511. That is an interview to a magazine, it's both English and B/C/S. Do you remember being interviewed in February 2006 by the "Nacional" magazine regarding your analysis?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they called me but I did not discuss with them. I turned down the offer of discussion with them. There was just a few sentences exchanged, some questions that were not very polite I would say, and then I just interrupted the conversation.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So your answer is yes, you remember this?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember and I know that they called me, but it was not an interview, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: If you could turn to page 3 of the English version and page 4 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Just give me the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Page 3. Just to confirm, are you in Exhibit 10511? Is that the exhibit before you? Thank you. So I'll direct your attention to page 3 of the English. Do you see that? If you go to the bottom of the page, the last complete paragraph you see that you were asked why so many years later someone finally came to the conclusion that you came to. And this was your response: "'This can be explained in only one way - that no one has, until now, carefully inspected the existing TV footage at the moment of the destruction of the Stari Most and immediately before its collapse. When you carefully examine the recorded material, it can be clearly seen that before the bridge collapsed, there was a water column that elevated along the length of the eastern bank, south of the bridge, and then you see black smoke at the foundation of the bridge. And it can immediately be explained that we are dealing with dynamite and an explosion at the foundation of the bridge on the eastern shore. I think that you do not require great expertise for this explanation.'" Do you remember saying that to them?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And again, you focused here on the timing. You talked in the second sentence about what happened immediately before the collapse. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, had the water pillar and explosion and the smoke and the light spot you spoke of, had those things happened the day before the collapse, so this would be 8th November, then there would not have been a high probability that those events caused the collapse on November 9th; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's logical.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was the close timing or the immediate proximity -- go ahead, you can answer.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry. You asked me whether there was a water pillar, whether there was a water pillar the day before. That would have meant that the bridge would not have been destroyed by an explosion. That was your question, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Would you mind repeating your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I will. Had the water pillar and the explosion and the smoke and the light spot that you spoke about, had those things happened the day before the collapse, so this would now be November 8th, would there then also be a high probability that those events that you spoke on -- of, they happened the day before, would have then caused the collapse the following day?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Had these events occurred one day before, they could not have destroyed the bridge the next day, that would be -- that's logical. However, however, the same events could have happened in the following day, it could be. I mean, that's the reason why I speak of a high degree of probability. I remain cautious as to the possibility of another explanation, but if there was a water wall one day and a collapse of the bridge the next day, there could have been a water wall the next day too.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, are you suggesting that it's possible that there was a water wall, water pillar, whatever you want to call it, that happened more than once?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely, because I can see that in the two videos and I'm not certain that the two films show one and the same event.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, that is your testimony now but that was not your testimony on direct; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't asked that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, when you were asked to write this opinion, that's not what your belief was, was it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you want me to answer? If you ask me a question, I try to answer it; that's all I can say. When we wrote our expert report we did not envisage such a possibility, such a hypothesis.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And now today as you testify, are you envisioning a different possibility, that being that these two videos are actually separate events?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Because of that, we could find similar reasons. That's why we spoke of high probability and not of a -- sort of a quasi certainty, as His Honour just asked.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So is the answer to that question yes?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I said what I said.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Let's look at the videos, Professor. The TV Mostar video is quite short, it's about 16 seconds long; and the TV ORF is a little bit over a minute.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Do you have that video in front of you on the screen? Do you recognise that to be the TV ORF video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: You will agree with me it's brownish in colour, there's writing on the bottom, and it appears to be taken from the west bank of the river?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And the vantage point is slightly to the south, you can see the east bank, and on the left portion of the screen you can see trees on the west bank. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with you. You can see part of the west bank, of the west bank, and it's more to the south -- oh, I have a map. It's about the same position as for the tank, same direction as the tank's direction and position.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay, Professor, we're going to run it the whole way through and then I'm going to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, sir, is this one of the videos upon which you based your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Let's go through it piecemeal. The very beginning, we're looking at the screen right now and it says November 8th on the bottom left-hand corner. You'll agree with me that's footage actually from the day before; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So we'll just go forward to the following day. You agree with me that this is November 9th?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It can't be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: We'll start it again, you can watch it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So are those the events upon which you based your opinion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So let's look at it a little bit more closely. Right there on the right-hand side of the screen, and for the record it's 1.5 on the counter, there was a splash in the water. What was the importance of that splash to you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Would you mind explaining again. I fail to understand you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This area on the right hand of the screen, that looks to be water; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the water gush or wall we spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. And it does appear from this angle to be a straight line; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, would you agree with me that seeing this video, I suggest it to you that perhaps a detonating cord was under water and that detonating cord caused the explosion?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And would you agree that this, what we see on the screen, resembles what you later tried to replicate in your experiment?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So I'm just going to change to the experiment video, and this is a 3D video.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Is this the experiment that you testified in direct testimony regarding?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And let's go back to the TV ORF video.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. So we just saw the water pillar. I'm going to play this again and I'm going to ask you to focus on the period of time right after the water pillar and look at the area under the bridge and tell me if you notice anything. Did you notice anything falling from the bridge? Professor, shall I play it again for you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: So we have it in slow motion, why don't we see it in slow motion?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So that was the fast motion and it's about to start in the slow motion, we're at 8.2. Here's the slow motion starting now. Now, there's the water pillar and I'm asking you to focus on anything falling from the bridge. And I'm going to stop right there, which is 29.9. Do you see something falling? What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I can see something falling, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to continue to play it and I'm going to ask you to tell me if you can see it splashing in the water. Did you see that splash?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. So if we start it again, did you just see the water pillar at 2.2?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And we continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And did you just see the splash a little earlier than 3.9?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I can see now the bridge collapsing.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I will start over again, it's very short. Do you see the water pillar?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Do you see the splash?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, what -- in order to establish a reference point, do you agree that the fall, whatever item that is, from the bridge and the splash come in the moments before we see the collapse? Do you agree that to be the case?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And for the record, the splash is at 3.3. I'm going to continue to play this so we can see the collapse.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the collapse comes immediately after the splash?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, but it also occurred after the water gush. Those two events occurred simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we'll go back to that, but I want to go back to the period of time where the bridge is falling into the water and ask that you focus on that. Now, in direct testimony you spoke about there potentially being two cameras. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And you testified that there was no continuity in this video; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And you would agree with me that there appears right before where it's stopped right now, at 4.4, there appears to be a cut or a splice or some sort of skip in the tape; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: There is a discontinuity with the segment when the bridge collapses, that's where discontinuity is visible on the video recording.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: That's exactly right. And I'm just going to continue to play this and you can look at the slow motion and we'll ask you another question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And right there at 34.2, we see the splash in the water. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And what follows is the collapse; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And at 41.1, the bridge appears almost -- almost all to be in the water; would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. However, it is difficult to say because there's a lot of water. We can't see exactly what there is.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, the period of time that you term as a discontinuity or the film is discontinuous, would you agree that at that moment there were events that we're not seeing on this film?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. That is the reason why I always used the other footage.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. But you testified on direct at page 31, line 12, that the most important frame is the frame that preceded the collapse. Is it now your testimony that that only means the TV Mostar video and not this video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. In the upper left-hand corner it says HRT; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please, so that we can be complete.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I stated that we need to view the frame preceding the collapse of the bridge. It is certain that there is continuity, we can see it on the second footage, but here there is discontinuity. I don't know what kind of discontinuity, I don't know what the reason for it is. However, in the second footage -- or rather, in the first footage, I can't see any projectile before the collapse of the bridge. There is none, not in the first footage nor in the second one. As for the second one, I can guarantee that there is continuity; as for the first one, there is discontinuity. The image is not continuous, but maybe there is time continuity. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Well, that being said, then you would agree with me that you cannot on this video, on the TV ORF video, see the frame that immediately preceded the collapse?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I repeat --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Can you answer that question yes or no, sir.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot answer your question with a simple yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Then let me ask you another question --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Can I give an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I repeat, there is discontinuity in the frames; however, this does not necessarily mean that there is no time continuity. It is possible that one footage was filmed and then the second was filmed from another camera, there were two cameras therefore. Those two footages could have been cut at the same moment, and maybe at the beginning of one footage was pasted which mean that the other one would continue. The cut happened at the same time. I believe that the interpretation is not right. I can try and explain that in English, but my English is not really good.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, we'll move on from here and we'll ask more questions about that so you can explain it. But I want you to look back at this TV ORF video and in the upper left-hand corner it says HRT, right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Is that a Croatian broadcast company or Croatian television company?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, those are the initials of Croatian TV.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And in the right-hand corner, upper right-hand corner, you see ORF2. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Is that an Austrian company?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Those are the initials of Austrian TV.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, are you aware that this is a video recording of a television set playing the HRT broadcast of a TV ORF news show?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, but I suppose so --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So in other words -- sorry, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I was under the impression that this was a broadcast by Austrian TV which was recorded by another TV. I don't know. I'm not an expert in those TV broadcasts.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Who gave you that impression?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it comes from Austrian TV.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: No, who gave you the impression, was it a person who put that in your mind or is it a result of watching the video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Upon watching the recordings, I can see that this is the frame of a television set. I was under the impression that a camera filmed the Austrian broadcast. That is my impression.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Professor, you would agree that the quality of this video is poor?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And it's very difficult to discern anything really specific by watching this clip; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Indeed, we had problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Did you make any efforts to enhance the video for a better analysis?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: We used our personal computers and we did a frame-by-frame analysis. We could reduce or maximise the image. Thanks to our personal computers we managed to enhance the quality.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Are you or either of your two colleagues who wrote this report video experts as well?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, we're not, but we asked a fourth colleague to come and help us out.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And is that fourth colleague's name on your report?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: No, because he was not qualified in that subject matter. He only helped us with computer work.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Just for the record, the TV ORF video, it's an IC number, and it's 820. I'm now going to show you Exhibit P 01040. We've looked at this during your direct testimony, and this was a video that was admitted into evidence on July 4th, 2007, and it's footage of the bridge that played on the television. Do you see that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And at the beginning we have November 8th again, this is the day before; correct? Professor, let me back that up and I'll repeat my question. The very beginning you're going to see some footage from the 8th of November. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. And now it turns to a vantage point that may look familiar to you. Does this look familiar?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It does, but this image and the previous frame, there is a discontinuity between the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Are you suggesting that between the November 8th and this footage there's discontinuity?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Yes, right. I will agree with you. Now, just tell me, this is in colour. The video you watched, it was not in colour; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And -- excuse me, I'll slow down. Does this vantage point look familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I would say it is the same, the same as the one from ORF2.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to play this for two minutes and then I will ask you some questions and I would just ask that you pay attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to stop it there at 6.15.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, is today the first time that you have seen this video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is the first time that I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. We're going to go back to the beginning. Again, this is November 8th, so it will just take a second to get to the following day, and I'm going to continue until you see the water pillar.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, is that the same water pillar you saw on the TV ORF video?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say whether it's the same water pillar, I don't know, but this is a similar water pillar. Here we can also see the dot of light. I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. So we're going to play it again. I'm going to ask you to look at the water pillar and then look at the area under the bridge for that item that falls.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see the splash?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, in the TV ORF video -- excuse me, I'm sorry. In the TV ORF video, you'll agree with me that the collapse came soon after that splash; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: It occurred afterwards, indeed, but a certain period of time elapsed between the two events, I don't know precisely how long.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to play this video for another minute, to 5.26, and then ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, a full minute has elapsed, we are at 5.26, and you will agree with me that the bridge has still not come down?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. And this video is different at least in that respect to the TV ORF video that you watched; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And, Professor, if you had seen this video before you wrote your opinion, would your opinion have been different?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, please let the witness answer the question. You will be given the floor afterwards, but please allow the witness to finish his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you will be given the floor later. At this crucial moment, however, please let the witness answer the question; afterwards, I will give the floor to you. Witness, please answer the question without taking into account what Mr. Praljak said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At any rate, if I'd had this video, I would have compared it carefully with the ORF video in order to see whether the ORF video, as I said before, is continuous in time, if there's a discontinuity in image, okay, but in time whether it was continuous and I would have had an answer. But for the time being look at all this, I can see the water gush, I can see the bridge which is intact; but let's not forget that the Mostar, TV Mostar video shows the water wall and continuously the fall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, General Praljak, what did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to tell the honourable Chamber, the witness, and the Prosecution this. If we look at the image the way it is, we can't determine whether it was edited, whether frames or shots were taken from and --

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, what you say is obvious. It could be put together and set up. I've thought of this too, but let Madam Prosecutor finish. You and your lawyer will be able to have redirect. Nothing rules out that frames may have been added without looking at the counter when you see 05.26.03. Please continue, Madam Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: I'm going to continue to play the video to 5.40, and I would ask that you focus your attention shortly before 5.40 at 5.38 and I'll ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, at 5.38 did you see what you've termed another discontinuity in the film?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN JANKOVIC
utterances.text: To carry out such an analysis I would need more time. I can't just do that in a minute. I can only give you bad answers. I need some peace and quiet, watch the video in order to answer such a question, otherwise I can't do it.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm going to show it to you one more time just so you can view it again and make one more attempt. I'm not going to forward it but we'll just let it run until 5.38.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you want to say, Mr. Kovacic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I object to this line of questioning. I object to the Prosecution's attempt to solicit the expert opinion by sight without having the possibility to go into the analysis frame by frame. And if you allow me to continue in Croatian, sorry. [Interpretation] The expert clearly explained, both during his evidence and in the written analysis, that the analysis was carried out frame by frame. That implied a certain set of conditions for them to be able to study the images that closely. Now the OTP are introducing another clip or recording. They want the witness's opinion on any discontinuity that may or may not be there. They're trying to compare this recording to the one that we showed the witness. They are leaving the witness in a situation where he's unable to say anything but simply I don't know. I would need to analyse more closely. On the other hand, in their indictment the OTP claimed that the HVO tore down that bridge. Given the burden of proof, they should have drawn up analysis themselves, brought a witness, or anything. They should have had a frame-by-frame analysis done outside the courtroom, because obviously it's impossible to conduct this sort of exercise in this courtroom. It's not something that he can do here. We ourselves had a number of plans with some further analyses and that sort of thing, but this just wasn't something that was doable in a courtroom setting. Thirdly, if only we had an opportunity here in this courtroom, equipped as it is, to play both recordings side by side, the ORF2 and the one that the Prosecutor has brought up, the images side by side, so we laymen could see if they're identical or not. But even so, it would still be necessary to have a technical frame-by-frame analysis for anyone to be able to say whether there is any continuity; whether there is a continuity of time; and thirdly, these two are identical or they are not identical. The Prosecutor now wants an analysis on sight in realtime and this is simply inappropriate, because the only choice that the witness has is to say: I don't know, I can't draw any conclusions. The witness is unable to show his expertise under these conditions. He's facing an impossible task. They would be much better off asking him, off the bat like that, to say what 9 might be to the power of 227.000. I think they would stand a much better chance of retrieving a reasonable answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 7.00, we have to stop now. We shall continue tomorrow with the cross-examination. I believe you have some time left. Witness, you are under oath. I remind you that you're no longer to have any contact with Mr. Kovacic because now you're a witness of the Court. You shall return to this courtroom tomorrow at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 1st day of July, 2008, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
